title: Step 0 (pair-absent) is enforced only in forge's local pass; once tx1 publicly reveals the seeder, an AM holder can pre-create the AM/sUSDS pair at an AM-cheap ratio, and seed() (amountBMin=0, F3) pours all 2,457.7 protocol-minted AM into it, where the attacker buys ~99.8% of it for 1e-6 sUSDS
severityNote: Working proposal Medium, borderline High. Fork-demonstrated theft of protocol value (~$2.3k at the seeded price; attacker +$1,320 realized / +$2,168 mark). Reachable only when a third party holds AM, i.e. Script A ran first. The runbook allows that order and Script A's audit makes it likely. Pre-A there are no AM holders, so the attack cannot happen.
disclosureQuote: story-113 L465: "[low] F3 (carried over): router add for AM/sUSDS uses amountBMin = 0, so on a skewed AM-cheap pair AM is paired against less sUSDS (unused sUSDS returns to lpRecipient)." story-122 L141: "F3: the AM/sUSDS add uses amountBMin=0. That is acceptable because the pair is created fresh in the same transaction, guaranteed by step 0."
disclosureGap: Both stories treat F3 as harmless: the unused sUSDS comes back, and step 0 is said to guarantee a fresh pair. Neither notes that (a) step 0 never runs on chain, and the broadcast has a 5-transaction gap between the public seeder CREATE and the seed; (b) the harm is not 'less sUSDS paired' but the protocol's AM sitting at a price the attacker chose, where the attacker buys it for nothing; (c) a private RPC does not close the gap, because tx1 is MINED publicly. Story-113 Decision 7 (L180) models only a donation ('A donor would give that AM to the LP holders'), not attacker-owned liquidity.
description: CutoverAntimatterPoolMainnet checks `factory.getPair(AM,sUSDS)==0` at Step 0 during forge's local simulation. With `--broadcast --skip-simulation --slow`, the six transactions then land one per receipt. tx1 deploys the seeder at a nonce-predictable address with all immutables visible, and the seed is tx5. On chain, AntimatterPoolSeeder.seed() handles an existing pair like this: if both reserves are non-zero, `_requireFullConsumption` reverts only when the AM is DEAR (susdsRequired > susdsOut); otherwise `_addLiquidity` calls Router02.addLiquidity(AM, sUSDS, am, susds, amountAMin=am, amountBMin=0). For an AM-cheap pair the router takes every unit of AM and only `am * rS/rA` sUSDS, and the rest goes back to OWNER. Nothing on chain bounds the price at which the protocol's AM enters the market.
impact: Fork at 26303964 (test_r44_02/03), post-Script-A world (a real staker claims, the attacker holds 1 AM). After tx1-4 land, the attacker createPair()s and mints LP with 1 AM : 1e-12 sUSDS. tx5 succeeds: it adds 2,457.703 AM and 2.46e-9 sUSDS, and returns 2,077.157 sUSDS to OWNER. tx6 (revoke) still lands. The attacker swaps 1e-6 sUSDS for 2,452.655 AM, annihilates them with 2,452.65 USDC into 4,905.31 phUSD, and sells into phUSD/sUSDS for 3,384.96 sUSDS. That is a realized gain of +$1,320, or +$2,168 holding the phUSD at spot. The protocol's new LP claims 6.05 AM plus 1e-6 sUSDS instead of 2,457.70 AM plus 2,077.16 sUSDS. Protocol loss: the 2,457.70 phUSD of POL burned, whose AM replacement went to the attacker (about $2,315 at the seeded price). The tax-neutral 'POL conversion' becomes a transfer to the attacker. The in-script post-conditions (all AM in the pair, OWNER holds LP) are not checked on chain and would hold anyway. The verifier passes, since it checks reserves > 0 and OWNER LP > 0 only.
evidence: side-effects.json adversarialRuns.midBroadcastFrontRun_amCheap_postA; logs/forktest-run44-antimatter.log (test_r44_02, test_r44_03); preA_world shows the vector needs AM held outside the protocol
recommendation: Enforce the precondition in the seed transaction itself. Pass an expected-fresh flag, or `minSUSDSPaired`, to seed(). The script would supply `susdsOut*(1-0.1%)` computed from the same pro-rata quote, or `require(amSusdsPair() == address(0))` when a fresh pair is intended, so that an AM-cheap pair makes tx5 revert (fail-loud) instead of leaking. Until then, run Script B strictly BEFORE Script A, while no third party can hold AM. Correct the runbook: a private RPC does not cover the tx1-to-tx5 window.

title: The 'always-run' minter revoke does not run when the seed failed and the AM/sUSDS pair exists: Step 0 aborts first, leaving the seeder an approved Antimatter minter
description: Story-122 L132 says 'The revoke (step 8) must always run, even on resume', and runbook L94 says 'B's minter revoke runs on every run.' If tx5 reverts after tx4 (setApprovedMinter(seeder,true)) has landed, --slow stops and tx6 is never sent. On re-run, Step 0 sees the existing pair. In the AM-dear front-run the attacker owns that pair and OWNER holds none of its LP, so the require reverts before Step 8 is reached. Every resume aborts the same way, and the grant stays in place indefinitely.
impact: Demonstrated (test_r44_04): after the AM-dear front-run makes tx5 revert AntimatterNotFullyConsumed, resume reverts at Step 0 and isApprovedMinter(seeder) stays true. Exploitability is nil today, because the seeder's only mint path is the onlyOwner seed() (test_r44_01). The harm is a stale privileged grant that the script's guard and runbook say cannot exist, so the owner must notice it and revoke by hand. A competent owner would be surprised (Law 3 footgun).
evidence: side-effects.json adversarialRuns.frontRun_amDear_postA; resumeMatrix row 'tx4 + tx5 REVERTED with foreign pair'
recommendation: Run the revoke before any abort. If a recorded seeder `isApprovedMinter`, revoke it first (or inside the Step-0 failure branch), then abort. Also state in the runbook that a tx5 revert requires a manual `setApprovedMinter(seeder,false)`.

title: [DISCLOSED, strengthened] An attacker can induce the seed failure and then spoof a resume to 'completed': with dust LP sent to OWNER, the resume skips the seed, the local-pass record says seeded=true, the patcher FILLs the attacker's pair and :verify passes
severityNote: Story-122 already labels this [medium]. That stands, on fork evidence that is stronger than the story's. No protocol funds are lost (the rescued slice stays on OWNER). The harm is a false-green pipeline that writes the attacker's pair into the book for Script C. It needs post-A AM.
disclosureQuote: story-122 Auto-Completed: "[medium] Script B step-0 resume branch is weaker than a fresh run: accepts any existing AM/sUSDS pair if the recorded seeder has code and OWNER holds any LP of it ... Crashed broadcast + griefer dust LP could make resume \"complete\" without seeding."
disclosureGap: The story says this needs a mid-broadcast crash plus active griefing, reduced by a private RPC. In fact the attacker can CAUSE the crash: an AM-dear pair created after tx1 makes tx5 revert, and the private RPC does not help (see AP-01). The story also did not note that the patcher and verifier then accept the state. The forge local pass already wrote deploymentStatus 'completed', seeded=true and simulated amMinted/liquidity to the progress file, so the patcher's 'completed && seeded' gate and the verifier's internal-consistency check both pass.
description: Step 0's resume branch accepts an existing pair if `p.seeder` has code and `IERC20(existing).balanceOf(OWNER) > 0`. It does not check `p.seeded` against the chain, compare against a recorded pair, or check any LP share.
impact: Fork (test_r44_04): after the AM-dear front-run and the tx5 revert, the attacker sends 1 wei of its LP to OWNER. The resume sends only the revoke and writes 'completed'. The 2,258.927 LP slice stays unconverted on OWNER, and the cutover mints no AM. VerifyAntimatterPoolCutover PASSES. The patcher (scratch copy of the book) FILLs AntimatterSusdsPair = 0xb6da… (the attacker's pair). The tax ledger would record a conversion that never happened. Script C would then wire UniswapHelper's AM routes to an attacker-priced pair.
recommendation: On resume, require chain evidence of THIS seed. Record the seed tx hash, or check `IERC20(existing).balanceOf(OWNER) >= p.liquidity` and `amReserve >= p.amMinted`, with OWNER's share of totalSupply above 99%. Never treat a progress record written in the local pass as proof that a transaction landed.

title: [DISCLOSED] VerifyAntimatterPoolCutover anchors no recorded figure to chain state: reserves > 0 and OWNER LP > 0 are the only live seed checks, so a never-seeded, foreign-priced pair verifies
disclosureQuote: story-122 Auto-Completed [low]: "Script B's verifier cross-checks recorded seed figures but not against chain receipts, and only logs the UniPoolerV2 LP decrement rather than asserting it."
description: The story's end-state checks (L135-140: phUSD burned == AM minted, pair AM reserve == AM minted, pooler LP − slice, OWNER holds the LP) reach the verifier only as checks on the record's internal consistency. Live checks never compare the pair's AM reserve or OWNER's LP share with the record, and never check the price.
impact: Demonstrated: the verifier passes on the AP-03 spoof, and on the AP-01 drained pool (OWNER LP > 0, reserves > 0). It cannot detect a pair created by someone else, wrong reserves, or a missing seed. It does catch an unrevoked minter (verifier L60-63).
evidence: test_r44_04 (verify passes on never-seeded state); side-effects.json postconditionResults
recommendation: Assert at least: OWNER's AM/sUSDS LP / totalSupply ≥ 99% (drift only from later third-party adds, which the verifier can bound), AM supply ≥ recorded amMinted, and a sanity band for pair price vs the phUSD/sUSDS price. Or read the seed tx receipt's Seeded event from broadcast/run-latest.json.

title: 1 wei of any of five tokens sent to the nonce-predictable seeder address blocks Script B at Step 9 (pre-deploy), or fails :verify permanently (post-deploy), because _requireSeederEmpty demands zero balances while the seeder itself tolerates pre-existing ones
function: _requireSeederEmpty (L156-163; called at Step 9 L426 and by the verifier L59)
description: The seeder's own `_requireUnchanged` compares before/after balances, so it tolerates tokens sent out of band (NatSpec L272-273: '...which rescueERC20 recovers'). The script and verifier instead require absolute zero balances of phUSD, AM, sUSDS, phUSD/sUSDS LP and AM/sUSDS LP. The seeder address is CREATE(OWNER, nonce), which is public: 0xdb70…09BE at nonce 1791.
impact: test_r44_09: 1 wei sUSDS sent to 0xdb70… before the run makes the preview/local pass revert 'end state: seeder holds sUSDS'. Nothing is broadcast, so the behaviour is fail-loud and safe, but B cannot run until the owner burns a nonce. test_r44_10: 1 wei sent after a completed run makes :verify revert until OWNER calls seeder.rescueERC20, which neither the script nor the runbook mentions. The cost to the griefer is negligible. Funds are never at risk.
recommendation: Compare seeder balances to their pre-seed values (as the contract does), or treat dust below a threshold as a warning. Document seeder.rescueERC20 as the remedy in the runbook.

title: Runbook and script NatSpec present a private RPC as the R1/F3 mitigation, but tx1 (seeder CREATE) is mined publicly 4 transactions before the seed under --slow
description: Flashbots Protect keeps pending transactions out of the public mempool. It does not hide mined ones. Under --slow, forge waits for each receipt, so the seeder deploy, rescue, approve and grant are each visible on chain (at least 4 blocks) before the seed is signed.
impact: The documented mitigation gives a false sense of safety for the AP-01/AP-03 window. On its own this is documentation, but it is the reason the operator would accept the A-before-B order.
evidence: side-effects.json executed.broadcastModeOnAnvil.txs (6 sequential receipts); entry-manifest broadcast flags
recommendation: State in the runbook that the private RPC protects only the seed tx's mempool exposure. Require B-before-A, or the on-chain guard from AP-01.
